rules.title: Berkeley ban on the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or manage occupancy (BMC ch. 13.63)
rules.requirement: Two acts are unlawful. (1) Selling, licensing or otherwise providing to Berkeley landlords a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley (§ 13.63.030(A)). (2) A landlord using such an algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley units (§ 13.63.030(B)). A coordinated pricing algorithm is any analytical or computational process that uses Competitor Data to calculate and recommend rents, fees, occupancy rates or other lease terms for future leases in coordination between a Berkeley landlord and one or more competitors, including through a third-party vendor. Competitor Data is non-public data on actual rents, occupancy and lease dates for other landlords' properties, when the data is less than 90 days old. For landlord use, each month a violation continues and each unit is a separate violation. The City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. An aggrieved tenant may sue over landlord use for injunctive relief, money damages and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. The prevailing City Attorney or tenant is awarded attorney's fees and costs, and a lease clause limiting tenant fees is unenforceable. The chapter does not regulate the amount of rent and does not bar general property-management software or tools using public data.
rules.key_value: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each unit is a separate violation; mandatory fee award to the prevailing City Attorney or tenant; Competitor Data = non-public data less than 90 days old

coverage.summary: Applies to all residential dwelling units in Berkeley, to landlords setting rents or occupancy there, and to vendors providing coordinated pricing algorithms to Berkeley landlords. No unit-count, building-age or landlord-size limits are stated. California's Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729) operates alongside this chapter.
coverage.other_conditions: The definition excludes (a) aggregated, anonymous rental data reports that make no recommendations; (b) products that set rent or income limits under government affordable-housing guidelines; (c) information used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development, provided Competitor Data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated.

rules.exemptions: Excluded from 'coordinated pricing algorithm': aggregated and anonymous reports that make no recommendations; affordable-housing rent or income limit tools; market research for project financing, appraisals, and software research, testing or training (Competitor Data may not be a live input at recommendation time).
rules.effective_date_note: The ordinance text (D001) has no effective-date clause and no final adoption date. It records only that the ordinance was passed to print on November 18, 2025 (8 ayes, 0 noes, 1 absent). The document URL refers to a December 2, 2025 Council item. The secondary alert DX06 (August 2026) lists the chapter as 'effective January 2026'. Under any of these dates the ordinance is in force on the query date.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies (BMC ch. 13.78)
rules.requirement:
Disclosure (BMC 13.78.010):
- Applies when an owner or agent charges a fee to buy a consumer credit report and to validate, review or process an application for Berkeley residential property.
- The owner must give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b).
- The disclosure must appear in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before the fee is received.

Renewal and roommate fees (BMC 13.78.016):
- An owner or agent may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, in whole or in part.
- This includes fees for a roommate's departure or for a request to add or replace a roommate.

Applicability (BMC 13.78.018):
- The chapter applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language.
- Lease provisions that violate it are unenforceable.
rules.key_value: Fee-rights statement and fee-cap disclosure before the fee is collected; no non-refundable renewal or roommate fees for existing tenants. The dollar cap is state law (Civ. Code § 1950.6); the Rent Board lists $68.96 for 2026.

coverage.summary: Applies to owners of Berkeley residential rental property and their agents, and to all residential rental agreements. It adds to the state fee cap, receipt and refund rules in Civ. Code § 1950.6 and does not replace them.

coverage.summary: Rent control (rent ceilings limited by the AGA) applies only to fully covered units: most multifamily units built before 1980, single-family homes with tenancies that began before 1996, and rooming houses (single-family homes with five or more rooms rented on separate leases). This includes units with Section 8, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC, HOME and similar subsidies. Partially covered units have registration and just cause but no rent control: new construction with a certificate of occupancy after June 1980, single-family tenancies from Jan 1, 1996, most condominiums and certain HUD subsidies. Where Berkeley's AGA applies, Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12 exempts the unit as housing under stricter local rent control. rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance just cause for eviction, notice requirements and owner move-in relocation assistance
rules.requirement:
Tenants in units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted without just cause (formerly called good cause). Measure BB made these changes:
- Nonpayment evictions require rental debt of at least one month's HUD Fair Market Rent for an equivalent unit in the Oakland-Fremont metro area.
- Tenants may not be evicted for failing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires.

Lease-breach evictions:
- The breached term must be mutually agreed.
- The breach must cause substantial actual damage to the landlord.
- The landlord must show the tenant's behavior was unreasonable.
- The prior notice to stop must specify the lease term and describe the violation and harm.

Notices and filings:
- Any termination notice must state that Rent Board advice is available and give the Board's counseling phone number and website.
- Copies of termination notices, notices to quit and summons and complaints must be filed with the Rent Board within three business days of service.
- For tenancies starting on or after Dec 20, 2024, landlords must give a Notice of Tenant Rights within 15 days of the tenancy start and post it in any interior common area.

Owner move-in relocation:
- Owners must pay relocation assistance for owner move-in evictions.
- The amounts are indexed to inflation and adjusted by the Rent Board every year, as Measure BB now requires.
- From Jan 1, 2026 the standard payment is $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households is $6,471, a 1.5% CPI-U adjustment approved on Oct 16, 2025.
rules.key_value: Nonpayment eviction only if debt is at least 1 month of HUD FMR; notices and lawsuits filed with the Rent Board within 3 business days; Notice of Tenant Rights within 15 days; owner move-in relocation $19,413 standard + $6,471 for qualifying households (from Jan 1, 2026)

rules.title: Berkeley Ellis Implementation Ordinance relocation assistance
rules.requirement: When an owner evicts tenants to remove a property from the rental housing market (Ellis Act withdrawal), the owner must pay the same relocation assistance as for an owner move-in eviction. The payments are indexed to inflation, and the Rent Board publishes the yearly increase. From Jan 1, 2026 the standard payment is $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households is $6,471. This is a 1.5% adjustment based on the San Francisco-Oakland-San Jose CPI-U.
